requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every uncovered item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every obligation in the subject has code that carries it out and a test that asserts the outcome. I did not trace the outline parser internals beyond what the tests exercise. The `habeas:none` form checks and the example-to-requirement trace are cited requirements, so I only checked that this code applies them.

**Parsing every first-party Rust file, except those under the root `vendor` directory**
- `rust_files` (src/rust_coverage.rs:312) keeps `.rs` files among the discovered sources and drops those under `<root>/vendor`. `validate_rust_functions` (:324) then iterates over them.
- Tests:
  - `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` checks that `vendor/dep`, `book/`, `evidence/`, `target/`, `.git` and nested `target` files are skipped. It also checks that `src/vendor` and `src/book` files are still validated.
  - `disallowed_paths_are_skipped_and_projects_outside_git_scan_every_file` checks that vendored Rust is not covered-checked.
  - `untracked_sources_are_not_validated_until_staged_and_status_lists_them` checks that untracked sources are skipped until staged.

**Functions, methods, trait methods, test helpers, structs, enums and unions must be covered**
- `item_kind` (:300) maps outline node kinds `fn`, `struct`, `enum` and `union` to reportable kinds. `unreferenced_items` (:234) lists every such node that is not cited.
- Tests:
  - `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, test helpers and nested fns.
  - `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside` covers structs, enums and unions.
  - `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` covers methods.

**Coverage by a valid reference**
- In `unreferenced_items`, `counts` accepts a `{impl}`, `{cite}` or `{test}` reference only to a defined requirement or to an example that traces to a requirement. It accepts a built-in only when `builtin.check(kind, fenced)` passes. It rejects `Term` and `Fixme` kinds and unknown names.
- References are read from comments via `outline.comments` and their `owner`, and from closed fenced comment fences. Nothing is read from string literals, enclosing modules or impl blocks, or evidence JSON. Comments inside a body count through the outline's comment-ownership rules.
- Tests:
  - Unknown names, string literals, enclosing `mod` and `impl` references, inner docs, trailing comments, body comments and blank-line runs are covered in `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references`.
  - Field and variant comments are covered in `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside`.
  - `an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement` covers the example-without-requirement, example-chained-to-example, example-citing-a-term and term-name cases.
  - `a_fixme_does_not_count_as_an_items_reference` covers `{fixme}`.
  - `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated` covers justified, inline, empty, wrong-role, unknown and unclosed `habeas:none` forms.

**Coverage by outline inputs in evidence records, citation reviews and site reviews**
- `EvidenceReads::load`, `add_record` and `covers` (:135–197) read all evidence files. They walk from the item up through its parent nodes and require a recorded selector with a matching current `structural_hash`.
- `inspect_repository_with_progress` (src/evidence.rs) loads reads from every evidence file, including citation and site reviews, and passes them to `validate_rust_functions`.
- Test: `items_an_assessment_read_with_their_current_hash_are_covered` covers an ordinary record, a citation review whose enclosing impl covers a method, a site review with a stale hash, and edits that make recorded hashes stale.

**Reporting every uncovered item and every parse failure**
- `uncovered_error` formats each uncovered item as `file:line: kind name is uncovered…`. A parse failure is reported as `file:line: cannot parse Rust source`, and the file is not skipped silently.
- Tests: `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures`, `discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference`, and `status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form` (reporting through status).
- `lost_items` (src/authoring/coverage_loss.rs) reuses `unreferenced_items` and `EvidenceReads::covers`. It is tested in `replacing_a_record_reviews_items_it_no_longer_covers_and_status_shows_the_result`.

**Named example must reference a requirement**
- `counts` applies `example_references_requirement`, and the test above covers it.

text: :::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every uncovered item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} discovery
Habeas MUST find the references of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a
name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped
roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST
consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in
the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in
both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git`
and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and
generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
:::{req} no_requirement
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this only when no requirement or example applies to the item under the
> reference procedure. The citation MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST
> justify why the item exists. An item with an invariant worth checking, such as
> a cache that must not change results, needs a requirement stating that
> invariant instead. An item citing this MUST NOT implement end-user-observable
> behavior that no requirement specifies.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it. Validation MUST report an inline citation of it
or a fenced citation whose body, without comment delimiters and other
references, is empty. Whether the justification holds MUST be assessed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. `habeas status --all` MUST list
each `habeas:none` citation with its item and justification.
:::{req} text_search
The harness MUST expose a `ripgrep` tool with this interface:
```text
ripgrep({ pattern: String, path: String = ".", context: Integer = 2,
referencing: Optional<ReferenceScope> }) -> SearchResult
ReferenceScope {
selection: String,                     // full name or definition glob
roles: Array<Role> = ["impl", "test", "cite"],
scope: "node" | "file" = "file",
SearchResult { matches: Array<SearchMatch> }
SearchMatch {
file: String,
item: String,        // selector of the innermost outline node
kind: String,
line_start: Integer, // the node's current lines
line_end: Integer,
lines: Array<{ line: Integer, text: String }>,
The tool MUST search the requested permitted file or directory using
ripgrep's regular-expression syntax and default case-sensitive search and ignore
rules. It MUST search in process using ripgrep's library crates, without
requiring an external `rg` executable, and MUST apply source-access policy while
walking files rather than filtering results afterwards. It MAY search files in
parallel; results MUST be ordered by path and then line regardless of
parallelism, so the same sources always produce the same inputs. Explicitly allowed paths and discovered generated-output directories MUST
be searched even when ignored or hidden; workspace disallow rules still apply.
Its model-facing description MUST explain those conventions. `context`
MUST be nonnegative and specify how many lines before and after each matching
line to include, defaulting to two on each side. Windows MUST stop at file
boundaries, and overlapping windows in the same file MUST be merged. The result
MUST give one entry for each innermost outline node containing a match, where a
match in a comment belongs to the node the comment belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`: the node's file, selector
under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, kind, and current line
range, and its matching and context lines with their line numbers, redacted
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. Search results MUST NOT become
evidence inputs and MUST NOT include definitions; the model-facing description
MUST tell the model to read with the `habeas` tool any node whose code its
conclusion relies on. Setting `context` to zero MUST return only matching lines.
With `referencing`, the tool MUST search only sources, within `path`, that carry
a reference in one of `roles` to a requirement or example the `selection`
matches under {cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`, including
anchors under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: with `scope` `node`, only
the outline nodes that contain or are named by those references, and with
`file`, their whole files. A selection matching no requirement or example, or an
unknown role or scope, MUST return an explanatory tool error. Its model-facing
description MUST explain `referencing`.
Search results MUST exclude files disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; explicitly requesting an excluded
path MUST be handled as a denial under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
No matches MUST return an empty array; invalid arguments or a failed search MUST
return an explanatory tool error.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
